messages:
maya: Heads up — `npm audit` on the Console UI build flagged a high-severity vuln in serialize-javascript after the latest deps update. Not sure if it lands in the shipped bundle but wanted to call it out.
ben: Can you paste the audit output? is it a transitive dep or direct?
maya: Output snippet:
```
  high serialize-javascript  >4.0.0  Remote Code Execution
  node_modules/serialize-javascript
  depends on vulnerable versions of serialize-javascript
  fix available via npm audit fix --force
  severity: high
```
maya: It's coming in through `webpack-dev-server` -> `serialize-javascript` (transitive). package-lock shows serialize-javascript@2.1.2 in the tree but audit says >4.0.0 is vulnerable? weird.
ben: Huh. The advisory we track affects older serialize-javascript versions used to deserialize untrusted input. We need to determine if our usage path exposes that code in production bundles. @carla any runtime concerns since Console is client-side React app?
carla: From infra side: console UI is statically served; exploit would require attacker-controlled payload that gets deserialized in users' browsers. If vulnerable code is only in devtools/webpack, risk might be low. But if it ends up in production bundle, then higher.
zach: I can grep the built artifacts for function names from serialize-javascript. Running `grep -R "serialize" build/` just to be sure.
maya: I ran a quick build — the production bundle includes a small helper from serialize-javascript. so yes it is bundled.
ben: OK we should triage as real. Options: upgrade serialize-javascript (major bump), adjust webpack to exclude bundling it, or sanitize inputs. Since it's transitive, easiest is to bump the direct dep that pulls it (maybe webpack-dev-server), or add a resolution override.
elena: Prefer minimal risk path: patch the lockfile with a resolutions override so the bundled version is safe, then run full QA and canary. We should avoid force-upgrading devtools that cause lockfile churn unless necessary.
maya: Proposed change (in package.json, using npm overrides):
```
  "overrides": {
    "serialize-javascript": "6.0.1"
  }
```
maya: Will update package-lock and open a PR with smoke test results.
ben: Tests we need: bundle integrity, spot-check SSO flows, CSP/nonce behavior, and a quick fuzz of any deserialization paths.
carla: Also suggest we coordinate with CDN cache invalidation — new bundle will need a clean rollout. Ops can do a staged deploy.
dependabot: I opened PR #482: bump serialize-javascript -> 6.0.1 (transitive override). CI: passes lint and unit tests, bundle size diff: +0.1%.
ben: Nice. @maya can you run the security smoke: build+serve, then run the grep/sanity that zach did, and attach bundle hash
maya: Done. Build hash: c1a3f7, grep shows no remaining matches to older serialize helpers. Manual quick check of eval/Function usage: none.
elena: What about lockfile churn? This override will modify package-lock.json — keep the PR focused and small. We'll avoid changing other deps in the same PR.
zach: I'll run the canary in staging and monitor error budgets for 24h. If nothing odd, we can push to production rollout with a 5% then 25% then 100% plan.
ben: Also file a short vuln ticket in our tracker with CVE link & decision (patched via override + rollout). Assign to maya, reviewer ben. Add labels: frontend, high-severity, needs-backport.
maya: Created TICKET-3145 with the details and links.
carla: Backport? Do we need to patch older release branches? The affected code path is present in v1.8 and v1.9 branches used by some customers.
elena: Yes — add backport to v1.9 and v1.8. maya, please open backport PRs (cherry-pick the override and lockfile change only).
maya: Will do today. Timeline: PR live now, staging canary in ~30m, if green we'll schedule prod rollout at 11:00 PDT. ETA to close TICKET-3145 after prod verification: EOD.
ben: Good. Postmortem notes: explain why devtool transitive dep landed in prod bundle; remind team to run `npm audit` as part of CI build step and add an ephemeral check that flags bundling of serialize-javascript.
zach: I'll add a CI job that greps production bundles for known unsafe patterns and fails the build if found. PR coming.
elena: Thanks all. Status: action items assigned, PR #482 open, TICKET-3145 created, staging canary running. :thumbsup:
maya: Thanks — ping me if you see anything in staging logs.

ops-bot: Deployment: staged rollout started for Console UI bundle c1a3f7 -> 5% traffic.
carla: Monitoring metrics: 30m in, no increase in error rates, no Sentry regressions.
zach: Canary looks clean at 6h. proceeding to 25% now.
ben: Closing loop: once at 100% update the ticket and mark as mitigated. Also keep the override documented in our dependency policy notes.
maya: Done — prod at 100% now. TICKET-3145 updated and moving to resolved. Thanks everyone! :tada:
